list_web_apps.title: List web apps in the subscription
list_web_apps.description: List every App Service site in the subscription -- web apps, function apps and containerised apps alike -- with each one's default hostname, state, App Service plan and runtime. The place to start when the resource group is not already known.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: Every site in the subscription.

items.description: id, name, kind, location and properties (state, defaultHostName, serverFarmId, httpsOnly, enabled).

list_web_apps_by_resource_group.title: List web apps in a resource group
list_web_apps_by_resource_group.description: List the App Service sites in one resource group with their state, hostnames and plans. Cheaper and more precise than scanning the whole subscription when the group is known.

resource_group.description: Name of the resource group.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The sites in the resource group.

get_web_app.title: Get a web app
get_web_app.description: Read one site's ARM resource -- its state (Running or Stopped), default and custom hostnames, App Service plan, outbound IP addresses, HTTPS-only flag, identity and availability state. Runtime settings such as the stack and always-on live in get_configuration, not here.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

app_name.description: Name of the web app or function app.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site resource.

kind.description: app, functionapp, app,linux and so on.

properties.description: state, defaultHostName, hostNames, serverFarmId, httpsOnly, outboundIpAddresses, siteConfig.

create_or_update_web_app.title: Create or replace a web app
create_or_update_web_app.description: Create a site, or replace an existing one's definition. A full PUT -- read the site with get_web_app, amend it, and send it back, or properties you omit are reset. server_farm_id points at the App Service plan the site runs on and is required on create; kind decides whether this is a web app ("app"), a Linux web app ("app,linux") or a function app ("functionapp").

resource_group.description: Resource group to create the site in.

app_name.description: Name of the site -- becomes the first label of its azurewebsites.net hostname, so it must be globally unique.

location.description: Azure region for the site. Must match its App Service plan's region.

server_farm_id.description: Full ARM id of the App Service plan the site runs on.

site_config.description: Runtime configuration -- linuxFxVersion or netFrameworkVersion, alwaysOn, appSettings, http20Enabled, minTlsVersion, healthCheckPath.

https_only.description: Redirect every HTTP request to HTTPS.

enabled.description: Whether the site serves traffic at all.

client_affinity_enabled.description: Pin a client to one instance with the ARR affinity cookie.

virtual_network_subnet_id.description: ARM id of the subnet to integrate the site's outbound traffic with.

public_network_access.description: Whether the site answers on its public hostname at all.

identity.description: Managed identity for the site, e.g. {"type": "SystemAssigned"}.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site resource as stored.

update_web_app.title: Update a web app
update_web_app.description: Merge changes into an existing site -- retag it, move it to another App Service plan, toggle HTTPS-only or enabled. Unlike the PUT form this leaves untouched properties alone, which makes it the right tool for a live site.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

app_name.description: Name of the site to update.

server_farm_id.description: ARM id of a different App Service plan to move the site onto.

https_only.description: Redirect every HTTP request to HTTPS.

enabled.description: Whether the site serves traffic at all.

client_affinity_enabled.description: Pin a client to one instance with the ARR affinity cookie.

site_config.description: Runtime configuration changes to merge in.

public_network_access.description: Whether the site answers on its public hostname.

tags.description: Replacement resource tags as key/value pairs.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site resource after the merge.

delete_web_app.title: Delete a web app
delete_web_app.description: Delete a site along with its slots, configuration and deployment history. Pass delete_empty_server_farm to also remove its App Service plan if nothing else is left on it. Not recoverable -- confirm the name with get_web_app first.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

app_name.description: Name of the site to delete.

delete_metrics.description: Also delete the site's historical metrics.

delete_empty_server_farm.description: Also delete the App Service plan if this was the last site on it.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty -- 200 when deleted, 204 when the site was already gone.

start_web_app.title: Start a web app
start_web_app.description: Start a stopped site so it serves traffic again. Takes effect within seconds; the first request afterwards still pays cold-start unless always-on is enabled in the site configuration.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

app_name.description: Name of the site to start.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.

stop_web_app.title: Stop a web app
stop_web_app.description: Stop a site so it serves nothing and returns 403 to callers. The App Service plan keeps charging -- billing is per plan, not per site -- so this takes an app offline rather than saving money.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

app_name.description: Name of the site to stop.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.

restart_web_app.title: Restart a web app
restart_web_app.description: Recycle the site's worker processes. Pass soft_restart to reload configuration without dropping in-flight requests, or synchronous to have the call wait until the restart has finished rather than returning at once.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

app_name.description: Name of the site to restart.

soft_restart.description: Reload configuration without interrupting in-flight requests.

synchronous.description: Wait for the restart to complete before returning.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.

list_app_settings.title: Get a web app's app settings
list_app_settings.description: Return the site's application settings -- the environment variables the app reads at runtime, including connection secrets and Key Vault references. A POST because the values are secrets. Read this before update_app_settings, which replaces the whole collection.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site's app settings as a name/value map.

properties.description: Every app setting, keyed by name.

update_app_settings.title: Replace a web app's app settings
update_app_settings.description: Write the site's application settings. This replaces the entire collection, so any setting missing from properties is deleted -- always call list_app_settings first, merge your change into what comes back, and send the whole map. Changing settings restarts the app.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

settings.description: The complete set of app settings as a name/value map. Anything absent is removed, so send everything list_app_settings returned plus your change.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The app settings as stored after the write.

list_connection_strings.title: Get a web app's connection strings
list_connection_strings.description: Return the site's connection strings with their values and types (SQLAzure, Custom, PostgreSQL and so on). A POST because the values are secrets. These are separate from app settings and are surfaced to the app with a type-specific prefix.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site's connection strings, keyed by name.

properties.description: Each entry with value and type.

update_connection_strings.title: Replace a web app's connection strings
update_connection_strings.description: Write the site's connection strings. Like app settings this replaces the whole collection, so read list_connection_strings first and send everything back. Each entry is an object with value and type.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

connection_strings.description: The complete set of connection strings, keyed by name, each an object with value and type. Anything absent is removed.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The connection strings as stored after the write.

get_configuration.title: Get a web app's runtime configuration
get_configuration.description: Read the site's runtime settings -- the language stack (linuxFxVersion, netFrameworkVersion), always-on, the startup command, health check path, minimum TLS version, HTTP/2, CORS rules, IP restrictions and worker count. This is the configuration that decides how the app runs, as opposed to the ARM resource that decides where it lives.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site's runtime configuration.

properties.description: linuxFxVersion, alwaysOn, appCommandLine, healthCheckPath, minTlsVersion, http20Enabled, cors, ipSecurityRestrictions, numberOfWorkers.

update_configuration.title: Update a web app's runtime configuration
update_configuration.description: Merge changes into the site's runtime settings -- change the language stack, turn always-on on, set a startup command or a health check path, tighten the minimum TLS version. A PATCH, so untouched settings are left alone. Most changes restart the app.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

configuration.description: Runtime settings to merge in, e.g. {"alwaysOn": true, "linuxFxVersion": "PYTHON|3.12", "healthCheckPath": "/healthz"}.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The runtime configuration after the merge.

get_diagnostic_logs_configuration.title: Get a web app's logging configuration
get_diagnostic_logs_configuration.description: Read where and at what level the site writes application logs, HTTP logs and failed-request traces -- filesystem, blob storage, or off. The first thing to check when logs are not appearing.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site's logging configuration.

update_diagnostic_logs_configuration.title: Update a web app's logging configuration
update_diagnostic_logs_configuration.description: Turn application logging, HTTP logging or failed-request tracing on or off and choose where they go. Filesystem application logging switches itself off after twelve hours by design, so use blob storage for anything you need to keep.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

logs_configuration.description: Logging settings, with applicationLogs, httpLogs, failedRequestsTracing and detailedErrorMessages blocks.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The logging configuration as stored.

list_publishing_credentials.title: Get a web app's publishing credentials
list_publishing_credentials.description: Return the site's SCM (Kudu) username and password -- the credentials for git deployment, the Kudu REST API and the advanced tools console. A POST because it returns a secret. These are disabled on sites where basic publishing credentials have been turned off.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site's SCM credentials and git deployment url.

get_publishing_profile_xml.title: Get a web app's publish profile
get_publishing_profile_xml.description: Return the site's publish profile as XML -- the file Visual Studio, the Azure CLI and the GitHub Actions deploy action all consume. It contains the deployment credentials in clear text, so treat the response as a secret.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

include_disaster_recovery_endpoints.description: Include the secondary region endpoints in the profile.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The publish profile, as an XML document containing deployment credentials.

list_deployments.title: List a web app's deployments
list_deployments.description: List the site's deployment history, newest first -- each with its id, status, author, deployment message and whether it is the currently active one. The audit trail for "what is actually running".

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site's deployments, newest first.

items.description: id, name and properties (status, message, author, deployer, active, start_time, end_time).

get_deployment.title: Get one deployment
get_deployment.description: Read a single deployment by id, with its status, the commit message and author, and the timestamps for when it started and finished. Use it to confirm which build is live after a release.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

deployment_id.description: Id of the deployment, from list_deployments.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The deployment record.

list_slots.title: List a web app's deployment slots
list_slots.description: List the site's deployment slots -- the parallel copies of the app used for staging -- each with its own hostname, state and configuration. Slots are what make a zero-downtime release possible via swap_slot.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site's deployment slots.

items.description: id, name (app/slot) and properties (state, defaultHostName, serverFarmId).

get_slot.title: Get a deployment slot
get_slot.description: Read one deployment slot as a site resource in its own right -- its hostname, state, plan and configuration. Use it to confirm a staging slot is healthy before swapping it into production.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The slot as a site resource.

swap_slot.title: Swap a deployment slot into production
swap_slot.description: Swap a slot with production, which is how App Service does a zero-downtime release: the staging slot is warmed up, then the routing is exchanged. Pass preserve_vnet to keep each site's virtual network settings in place rather than swapping those too. Slot-sticky settings stay where they are; everything else moves.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

target_slot.description: Slot to swap into production, e.g. staging.

preserve_vnet.description: Keep each site's virtual network configuration where it is instead of swapping it.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty; the swap runs asynchronously and reports through the location header.

list_functions.title: List a function app's functions
list_functions.description: List the functions in a function app, each with its trigger bindings, script path, invoke url template and whether it is disabled. Returns an empty list on an ordinary web app.

resource_group.description: Resource group the function app is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The functions in the app.

items.description: id, name and properties (config with bindings, script_href, invoke_url_template, isDisabled).

get_function.title: Get one function
get_function.description: Read a single function's definition -- its bindings, script location, invoke url template and disabled state. Use it to work out what a function is triggered by before calling it.

resource_group.description: Resource group the function app is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The function's definition.

list_function_keys.title: Get a function's access keys
list_function_keys.description: Return the keys that authorise calls to one HTTP-triggered function. These go in the x-functions-key header or the code query parameter. A POST because the values are secrets.

resource_group.description: Resource group the function app is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The function's keys, keyed by name.

list_host_keys.title: Get a function app's host keys
list_host_keys.description: Return the function app's host-level keys -- the master key, which can invoke anything and manage the app, and the default host key, which works across every function. The master key is effectively an admin credential, so handle the response accordingly.

resource_group.description: Resource group the function app is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The app's host keys.

masterKey.description: Admin-level key; can invoke and manage everything.

list_processes.title: List a web app's running processes
list_processes.description: List the worker processes running on the site, each with its process id, name, memory and CPU usage and start time. The closest thing this API has to a live look at what the app is doing.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site's running processes.

items.description: id, name and properties (start_time, total_cpu_time, private_memory, thread_count).

list_custom_hostname_bindings.title: List a web app's hostname bindings
list_custom_hostname_bindings.description: List the hostnames bound to the site, each with its SSL state and the certificate thumbprint serving it. Where to look when a custom domain is serving the wrong certificate or none at all.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The hostnames bound to the site.

items.description: name and properties (hostNameType, sslState, thumbprint, customHostNameDnsRecordType).

get_source_control.title: Get a web app's source control configuration
get_source_control.description: Read where the site deploys from -- the repository url, branch, and whether continuous deployment and the App Service build service are enabled. Empty on a site deployed by zip push or container image instead.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site's source control configuration.

update_source_control.title: Connect a web app to a repository
update_source_control.description: Point the site at a git repository and branch for deployment. With is_manual_integration false, App Service sets up a webhook so every push to the branch deploys -- which means this call can start shipping code automatically.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

branch.description: Branch to deploy. Defaults to the repository's default branch.

is_manual_integration.description: True to require a manual sync; false to deploy on every push via a webhook.

deployment_rollback_enabled.description: Allow rolling back to a previous deployment.

is_github_action.description: Set when a GitHub Actions workflow, not App Service, does the building.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The source control configuration as stored.

sync_repository.title: Trigger a deployment from the repository
sync_repository.description: Pull and deploy the configured branch now. This is the manual trigger for a site set up with is_manual_integration -- it deploys whatever the branch currently holds, so it ships code.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

app_name.description: Name of the site to deploy.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.

list_backups.title: List a web app's backups
list_backups.description: List the backups taken of the site, each with its status, size, the blob it was written to and which databases it included. Read this before a restore to find the backup id you want.

resource_group.description: Resource group the site is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The site's backups.

items.description: id, name and properties (status, sizeInBytes, created, storageAccountUrl, databases).

list_app_service_plans.title: List App Service plans
list_app_service_plans.description: List the App Service plans in the subscription with each one's SKU, worker size, instance count, operating system and how many sites it hosts. Plans are what App Service actually bills for.

detailed.description: Include each plan's site count and other computed properties.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: Every App Service plan in the subscription.

items.description: id, name, location, sku and properties (numberOfSites, status, reserved, maximumNumberOfWorkers).

get_app_service_plan.title: Get an App Service plan
get_app_service_plan.description: Read one plan's SKU and tier, instance count, operating system (reserved true means Linux), zone redundancy and how many sites run on it. Check this before adding a site, since the plan sets the resource ceiling every site on it shares.

resource_group.description: Resource group the plan is in.

plan_name.description: Name of the App Service plan.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The App Service plan resource.

sku.description: name, tier, size, family and capacity.

create_or_update_app_service_plan.title: Create or scale an App Service plan
create_or_update_app_service_plan.description: Create a plan, or change an existing one's tier or instance count -- which is how App Service scales up (a bigger sku) and out (more capacity). Every site on the plan is affected. Set reserved true for a Linux plan; it cannot be changed afterwards.

resource_group.description: Resource group to create the plan in.

plan_name.description: Name of the App Service plan.

location.description: Azure region for the plan, e.g. westeurope.

sku_name.description: SKU code, e.g. F1, B1, S1, P1v3, EP1 for Elastic Premium, Y1 for Consumption.

sku_tier.description: Tier name matching the SKU, e.g. Free, Basic, Standard, PremiumV3.

capacity.description: Number of instances to run. This is how the plan scales out.

reserved.description: True for a Linux plan, false for Windows. Immutable after creation.

per_site_scaling.description: Let each site on the plan scale independently rather than together.

zone_redundant.description: Spread instances across availability zones. Needs at least three instances.

maximum_elastic_worker_count.description: Instance ceiling for an Elastic Premium plan.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The plan resource as stored.

delete_app_service_plan.title: Delete an App Service plan
delete_app_service_plan.description: Delete an App Service plan. The call fails while any site still runs on it, so move or delete those first -- check numberOfSites with get_app_service_plan.

resource_group.description: Resource group the plan is in.

plan_name.description: Name of the plan to delete.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty -- 200 when deleted, 204 when the plan was already gone.

check_name_availability.title: Check whether a site name is free
check_name_availability.description: Ask whether a proposed site name can be used. Site names are globally unique because they become the azurewebsites.net hostname, so check before create_or_update_web_app rather than after it fails.

type.description: Resource type the name is for.

is_fqdn.description: Set when name is a fully qualified domain name rather than a bare site name.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: Whether the name is free, and why not when it is taken.

list_geo_regions.title: List regions App Service is available in
list_geo_regions.description: List the Azure regions App Service serves, optionally narrowed to those offering a particular SKU or Linux workers. Use it to find a valid location before creating a plan.

sku.description: Only return regions offering this SKU, e.g. PremiumV3.

linux_workers_enabled.description: Only return regions that offer Linux workers.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The regions App Service is available in.

list_web_app_stacks.title: List available runtime stacks
list_web_app_stacks.description: List the language runtimes App Service supports, with each version's settings, whether it is a preview, and when it goes out of support. This is where a valid linuxFxVersion or netFrameworkVersion value comes from.

stack_os_type.description: Narrow to the stacks available on one operating system.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The supported runtime stacks and their versions.

items.description: name, displayText and properties.majorVersions with minorVersions and runtime settings.

list_certificates.title: List App Service certificates
list_certificates.description: List the certificates in the subscription available to App Service, with each one's subject, thumbprint, issuer and expiry. The place to check when a custom domain's TLS certificate is about to lapse.

api_version.description: Microsoft.Web ARM API version to call.

output.description: The certificates available to App Service in the subscription.

items.description: id, name, location and properties (subjectName, thumbprint, issuer, issueDate, expirationDate, hostNames).
